name: coulomb-from-crossing-counts
description: Corrects the scope of CrossingCountAffine: it excludes the LINEAR class only, and Z(Z-1) is reachable from the crossing counts quadratically — 16·Z(Z-1) = (n+ - n-)(n+ - n- - 4) exactly, on 16 nuclei. The A^(1/3) scale is the cube root of the extensive unsigned channel n+ + n- = 10A-2, which needs no hyperbolic structure — the volume route is closed by measurement (0 of 40 branch closures hyperbolic). Assembled, Z(Z-1)/(n+ + n-)^(1/3) tracks the mirror Coulomb displacement energy across A=3..39 with one slope. Scope (a); the slope is NOT derived and nothing is wired.

assertions.name: n+ + n- = 10A - 2 and n+ - n- = 4Z on all 16
assertions.detail: exact integer equality on every row; the unsigned channel depends on A alone (mirror-invariant) and the signed one is 4Z.

assertions.name: the counts are over the ADJACENT-PAIR CHAIN (A-1 bonds), not the free-nucleon word
assertions.detail: atom_braid_word_3A's include_inter defaults to True (verified by CALLING it, on A = 2,4,6,8, not by reading the signature), and the default word length is exactly 12A - 1 = (n+ + n-) + n_averaged = (10A - 2) + (2A + 1). So the channel is affine in A because the bond set is a CHAIN, not because there are no pair bonds. Same A-1 chain as binding_canonical.py and QOU.Mass.SelfMutualPartition. Had they come from the complete-graph builder (C(A,2), quadratic in A), §2's 'one degree up' would be reachable linearly instead.

assertions.name: the proton-pair multiplicity IS a quadratic in the counts
assertions.detail: exact on all 16 in integer arithmetic. CrossingCountAffine excludes a·n+ + b·n- + c = Z(Z-1) for CONSTANT a,b,c — the affine class. This is one degree up and it lands exactly. The ingredient was never excluded; only the linear closure was.

assertions.name: the linear exclusion is untouched — both statements hold at once
assertions.detail: Z(Z-1) has second difference 2 while every linear combination has 0, so no linear form matches; and the quadratic form matches at every Z. Nothing is contradicted — a boundary is located.

assertions.name: no hyperbolic volume exists at the atom-braid level to take a root of
assertions.detail: 0 of 40 branch closures are hyperbolic across p, n and the deuteron — every one degenerate. So `Vol(K_A)^(1/3)` as the A^(1/3) scale is blocked by a measured fact, not by preference. This is read from the committed witness, not re-derived.

assertions.name: the cube root is IMPOSED, not derived — it tracks A^(1/3) trivially
assertions.detail: ratio spans 2.0800838 .. 2.1507456 (spread 0.0706618) over A=2..39, tending to 10^(1/3) = 2.15443469. 🛑 THIS IS NOT A DERIVATION AND MUST NOT BE READ AS ONE: the exponent 1/3 is written in BY HAND. Since n+ + n- = 10A - 2 is affine in A, (n+ + n-)^(1/3) is A^(1/3) with extra steps, and the near-constant ratio is arithmetic. Bean qou-nf9l (COMPLETED) refuted all three corpus combinatorial classes for producing a cube root of A, and its census records that every 1/3 in the corpus is a FIXED INDEX 3, never an A-th root. The only thing this section adds is that the count channel is available where the hyperbolic volume is not (0 of 40 branches).

assertions.name: the assembled shape tracks the mirror Coulomb energy across A=3..39
assertions.detail: R^2 = 0.99809392 on 5 mirror pairs spanning A = 3..39, with a single slope and no other free quantity. Compare qou-vudb, where the model's mirror asymmetry was a CONSTANT (A^0) against an observed A^0.87. Scope (a): 5 points, one fitted slope, and the slope is NOT derived — this measures shape agreement, not a derivation.

assertions.name: section 4 does NOT test the quadratic — it cancels in a mirror pair
assertions.detail: ΔZ(Z-1) = A - 1 exactly on all 5 pairs, so section 4's shape is (A-1)/(10A-2)^(1/3), a pure function of A. Its R^2 against another function of A is near-guaranteed and is NOT evidence for the quadratic multiplicity. What section 4 CAN test is the EXPONENT.

assertions.name: the data prefers p = 1/4, NOT 1/3 — reproducing qou-nf9l independently
assertions.detail: minimised at p = 1/4 (rel spread 0.12131); 1/3 is nearly double that. This INDEPENDENTLY REPRODUCES the corpus's own 8-pair fit p* = 0.252 +- 0.020 (docs/audits/2026-07-13-packing-exponent-combinatorics-derive-or-refute.md, bean qou-nf9l), where 1/4 sits at 0.1 sigma and 1/3 at 4.1 sigma — a different sample and a different method, same answer. So the SEMF's A^(1/3) is not what this data wants. p = 0 (the current model's behaviour, no length scale at all) is much worse than either. Scope (a), 5 points, one scanned parameter; evidence about the DENOMINATOR only — the quadratic numerator cancels here by construction.
